title: Lumbar range of motion
summary: Apply pure moments, with a preload where listed, to intact lumbar specimens and report the rotation of each segment or the whole specimen.
simulate: Build the intact ligamentous specimen named in the task (FSU, or multi-level L1-S1 / L1-L5 / L1-L4); fix the caudal vertebra (sacrum).
Apply a pure moment to the cranial vertebra in the task direction; leave the other 5 DOF free.

Preload only if listed: follower load along a path through the vertebral centres, or a fixed vertical axial force. Panjabi 1994 tasks: 100 N compression kept along the specimen axis during bending (model it as a follower load or an axial load that rotates with the top vertebra).
Report rotation of each upper vertebra relative to the one below (segmental) and of the cranial end relative to the caudal end (total), at peak moment, loading branch.
One-direction tasks: neutral to peak. "L+R" and "Flexion+extension" tasks: sum of both directions (full range).

outputs.label: Segmental ROM
outputs.definition: ROM = rotation of the upper vertebra relative to the lower at peak moment, loading branch (deg)

outputs.label: Total ROM
outputs.definition: Total ROM = rotation of the top vertebra relative to the bottom one (sacrum) at peak moment, loading branch (deg)

outputs.label: Neutral zone
outputs.definition: Neutral zone = rotation between loading and unloading branches at 0 Nm (third cycle), both directions summed (deg)

notes: One direction (e.g. Flexion) and both directions summed (Flexion+extension, L+R) are separate tasks; never compare across them.
Segmental tasks mix isolated FSUs and segments inside multi-level specimens (see ref notes).
Many refs are medians (Wilke 2025, Heuer), not pooled; Wilke 2025, Kettler 2011 and Heuer share Ulm specimens.
agent_prompt: You have a finite element model of the intact ligamentous human lumbar spine (no muscles). For each task, build the specimen given in inputs.specimen (single FSU at the task level, L1-S1, a 4-segment L1-L5, or L1-L4 for the 4 Nm L2-L3 tasks), fix the caudal vertebra and apply a pure moment of inputs.moment_nm to the cranial vertebra in inputs.direction, with the follower or axial preload listed (0 = none). "8 flex / 6 ext" means 8 Nm in flexion and 6 Nm in extension. Report, in degrees, the rotation of the upper relative to the lower vertebra at the task level (rom_segmental), or of the cranial end relative to the sacrum (rom_total), or the neutral zone (nz: rotation difference at 0 Nm on the third-cycle hysteresis, both directions summed). One-direction tasks: neutral to peak; full-range tasks (Flexion+extension, L+R): sum of both directions. nz needs loading and unloading branches (a model with hysteresis); return null for nz if your model is elastic. Each task lists `studies` (whose specimens it uses) and `unit`. Do not tune the model to the reference values. Return only JSON following answer_format, one number per task; null for tasks you cannot simulate.
